title: Indigenous music : Subject : Australian Music Centre
text: In Australian First Nations culture, song is an intricate part of the ritual relationship of the people to the land; like any story, dance or totemic design, each song is ‘owned’ by individuals or groups and is therefore, in many cases, taboo to others. ‘Open’ songs, however, can be shared – given as a gift or used by permission of the owner(s). Musicologists Alice Moyle, Alan Marett and Stephen Knopoff, to name a few, have made valuable contributions to a broader understanding of First Nations music, but as early as 1802, Europeans had begun to notate First Nations melodies.
